plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A showpiece of the fynbos. Each flower head is a bowl of silky, pointed bracts, ringed around a center of fuzzy, pale florets. The heads can grow as wide as a dinner plate. They sit on tough, leathery-leaved shrubs on the slopes of the Cape.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter and spring, June to October, so it is in full flower in early September.
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa (for example, the fynbos of Table Mountain and Kirstenbosch)
plants.funFact: It is South Africa's national flower. The plant has evolved to survive regular wildfires. It resprouts from an underground woody base after the fire passes.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Late winter brings a haze of golden color to the Australian bush. Branches are covered in fluffy, sweetly scented pompom flowers. Silvery-green, sickle-shaped leaves lie beneath them. Native bees and birds crowd the trees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, typically August to September, which makes it a fitting plant for early September in the southern hemisphere.
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: It is Australia's floral emblem. National Wattle Day is held on 1 September to mark the start of spring.

plants.name: Rudbeckia hirta
plants.description: A cheerful daisy-like flower with golden-yellow rays around a dark, domed brown center. It lights up meadows, roadsides and garden borders. Bees and butterflies visit it until the first frosts.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring through early autumn, roughly May to September and often into October, so it is still blooming on September 9.
plants.location: Native to central and eastern North America, and widely grown in gardens across the continent
plants.funFact: This plant is a biennial or short-lived perennial. It readily self-seeds, so a few plants can grow into a large drift of blooms within a few years.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped flowers rise straight from bare soil. They appear without any leaves, which gives them a ghostly look in late-summer meadows and borders. The leaves emerge the following spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer into autumn, roughly August to October, so it is in bloom in early September.
plants.location: Meadows and gardens across Europe and temperate regions; native range extends from Europe into Asia Minor and the Caucasus
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is not a true crocus. All parts of the plant are highly toxic. It contains colchicine, a compound that gardeners and plant breeders also use to alter plant chromosomes.
